classification.difficultyReason: Sketch eight linear half-planes, selecting the correct shaded side and distinguishing included and excluded boundaries.

answer.short: Shade above the dashed line $y=x+2$, through $(-2,0)$ and $(0,2)$. Exclude the boundary.
answer.worked: Draw the boundary $y=x+2$ through $(-2,0)$ and $(0,2)$. Use a dashed line because the inequality is strict. At $(0,0)$, $0>2$ is false, so shade the side away from the origin: above the line.

spec.description: Dashed boundary through the two intercepts; the upper half-plane is shaded.

answer.short: Shade above the solid line $y=2x-4$, through $(0,-4)$ and $(2,0)$. Include the boundary.
answer.worked: Draw the boundary $y=2x-4$ through $(0,-4)$ and $(2,0)$. Use a solid line because equality is included. At $(0,0)$, $0\geq-4$ is true, so shade the side containing the origin: above the line.

spec.description: Solid boundary through the two intercepts; shade above it, including the origin.

answer.short: Shade above the dashed line $y=2-x$, through $(0,2)$ and $(2,0)$. Exclude the boundary.
answer.worked: Draw the boundary $y=2-x$ through $(0,2)$ and $(2,0)$. Use a dashed line because the inequality is strict. At $(0,0)$, $0>2$ is false, so shade the side away from the origin: above the line.

spec.description: Dashed descending boundary through the two intercepts; shade above it.

answer.short: Shade below the solid line $y=6-2x$, through $(0,6)$ and $(3,0)$. Include the boundary.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x+y&\leq6\\y&\leq6-2x\end{align*}$$
Draw the solid boundary through $(0,6)$ and $(3,0)$. At $(0,0)$, $2(0)+0\leq6$ is true, so shade the side containing the origin: below the line. Include the boundary.

spec.description: Solid descending boundary; shade below it, including the origin.

answer.short: Shade above the dashed line $y=3-\frac32x$, through $(0,3)$ and $(2,0)$. Exclude the boundary.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3x+2y&>6\\2y&>6-3x\\y&>3-\frac32x\end{align*}$$
Draw the dashed boundary through $(0,3)$ and $(2,0)$. At $(0,0)$, $3(0)+2(0)>6$ is false, so shade the side away from the origin: above the line. Exclude the boundary.

spec.description: Dashed boundary with intercepts 2 and 3; shade above it.

answer.short: Shade below the solid horizontal line $y=-1$. Include the boundary.
answer.worked: Draw a solid horizontal line through $(0,-1)$. The inequality requires $y$ to be at most $-1$, so shade below the line and include it.

spec.description: Solid horizontal boundary at minus one with the lower half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade left of the dashed vertical line $x=-1$. Exclude the boundary.
answer.worked: Draw a dashed vertical line through $(-1,0)$. The inequality requires $x$ to be less than $-1$, so shade to the left of the line and exclude it.

spec.description: Dashed vertical boundary at minus one with the left half-plane shaded.

answer.short: Shade below the solid line $y=3x$, through $(0,0)$ and $(1,3)$. Include the boundary.
answer.worked: Draw the solid boundary $y=3x$ through $(0,0)$ and $(1,3)$. Test $(1,0)$, which is not on the boundary: $0\leq3$ is true. Shade the side containing $(1,0)$, below the line, and include the boundary.

spec.description: Solid boundary through the origin and labelled point (1,3); shade below the boundary.
